headline: Storm Adam floods towns on Spain's east coast

sources.title: Four dead as torrential rain batters eastern Spain (Al Jazeera)
At least five killed and thousands evacuated as Storm Adam batters eastern Spain (Euronews)
Pedro Sanchez to visit Valencia village left 'upside down' by deadly Storm Adam as 280 were rescued by helicopter and 2,100 evacuated (The Olive Press)

chunks.text: Storm Adam caused [[severe flooding]] in eastern Spain in October 2026. Heavy rain {{set in}} on Saturday, October 17. Some towns in the Valencia and Alicante areas got more than 600 millimeters of rain, or about 24 inches, in 24 hours. Rivers [[overflowed]], and many streets were [[under water]]. The floods {{washed cars away}} and {{cut off}} several towns. News reports on October 20 counted at least four deaths. Some reports counted five.

verbs.correct: To begin and seem likely to last
verbs.wrong: To fall only in a small area
verbs.why: Cold weather sets in early in the mountains. In some places, the rainy season sets in each June. Heavy rain set in on Saturday, October 17, along Spain's eastern coast.

verbs.correct: To move something with the force of water
verbs.wrong: To fill something with river water
verbs.why: Heavy rain often washes the soil away on this hill. A big wave sometimes washes small boats away. The floods washed cars away in several towns.

verbs.correct: To make a place impossible to reach
verbs.wrong: To send help to a place by air
verbs.why: Deep snow cuts off our village every winter. Floods often cut off farms near the river. The floods cut off several towns in eastern Spain.

chunks.text: Emergency services {{carried out}} about 500 rescues in the Valencia region, a government official said. In one [[coastal town]], helicopters lifted about 280 people to safety, many from [[rooftops]]. In Alicante province, rescuers {{pulled 13 people out}} of their cars after a tunnel flooded. The government also {{brought in}} its [[military emergency unit]]. More than 2,100 people were [[evacuated]]. A [[public shelter]] in the [[hardest-hit]] town {{took in}} about 400 people overnight.

verbs.correct: To do a planned task or job
verbs.wrong: To count the number of people
verbs.why: Firefighters carry out safety checks every month. The team carries out a test before each trip. Emergency services carried out about 500 rescues in the Valencia region.

verbs.correct: To remove someone from a place
verbs.wrong: To check that someone is not hurt
verbs.why: Lifeguards pull swimmers out of strong waves. Firefighters sometimes pull drivers out of crashed cars. Rescuers pulled 13 people out of their cars after a tunnel flooded.

verbs.correct: To ask a group to come and help
verbs.wrong: To give a group new orders
verbs.why: The city brings in extra workers after big storms. Schools bring in experts when there is a serious problem. The national government brought in its military emergency unit.

verbs.correct: To give people a place to stay
verbs.wrong: To move people to a safer town
verbs.why: The church takes in families who lose their homes. Animal shelters take in lost dogs. A public shelter took in about 400 people overnight.

chunks.text: On Monday, October 19, officials told people in about 145 towns to {{stay in}}. They asked people to avoid travel and move to [[upper floors]]. The regional government {{sent out}} [[emergency alerts]] to cell phones over the weekend and on Monday. The alerts told people to {{stay away}} from rivers and to move to [[higher ground]]. Classes were [[canceled]] for more than 100,000 students. By Monday afternoon, most of the [[restrictions]] had ended.

verbs.why: We stay in on cold, rainy nights. Many people stay in when the roads are icy. Officials told people in about 145 towns to stay in on October 19.

verbs.correct: To deliver a message to many people
verbs.wrong: To check a message for mistakes
verbs.why: The school sends out a text when classes are canceled. The city sends out warnings before a big storm. The regional government sent out emergency alerts to cell phones.
Doctors tell sick people to stay away from crowds. Good swimmers stay away from the rocks. The alerts told people to stay away from rivers.

chunks.text: The floods {{brought back}} [[painful memories]] of October 2024. Back then, floods killed more than 230 people in the Valencia region. Officials faced [[criticism]] for late phone warnings. The rain began to {{die down}} on Tuesday, October 20. Spain's prime minister planned to visit the flooded coast that day. The national weather agency kept warnings in place for nine [[provinces]]. It asked people in Catalonia and the Balearic Islands to {{watch out for}} more heavy rain.

verbs.wrong: To make you angry about something
verbs.why: This song brings back happy memories of my childhood. Old photos bring back memories of our first home. The floods brought back painful memories of the deadly floods in October 2024.
The wind usually dies down at night. The noise dies down when the teacher arrives. The rain began to die down on Tuesday, October 20.

verbs.correct: To be careful about a danger
verbs.wrong: To report a danger to others
verbs.why: Drivers watch out for ice on winter roads. Hikers watch out for snakes in the summer. The weather agency asked people in Catalonia and the Balearic Islands to watch out for more heavy rain.

mainIdea.s: Storm Adam brought extreme rain to eastern Spain, flooding towns and killing at least four people. Officials sent early phone alerts, unlike in 2024, and warnings moved north to Catalonia.
mainIdea.why: Rescuers carried out hundreds of rescues after the floods. This time the regional government sent out alerts over the weekend, and Catalonia and the Balearic Islands stayed on alert.

mainIdea.s: Heavy rain from Storm Adam flooded Spain's eastern coast and killed several people. Many residents were angry because the phone warnings reached them only after the water had risen.
mainIdea.why: Close, but the regional government sent out phone alerts over the weekend and again on Monday. The late warnings were a problem in the 2024 floods.

mainIdea.s: A long, dry summer has left farms in southern Spain with very little water. Officials asked towns to limit how much people use for gardens and pools until the fall rains finally arrive.
mainIdea.why: Storm Adam brought floods, not a dry summer. Its very heavy rain cut off several towns on the coast of eastern Spain.

tf.s: Heavy rain set in along Spain's eastern coast.
tf.why: Heavy rain set in on Saturday, October 17, and some towns got more than 600 millimeters in 24 hours.

tf.s: No one died in the floods from Storm Adam.
tf.why: At least four people died after the floods washed cars away and cut off towns.

tf.s: Officials sent out phone alerts only after the storm ended.
tf.why: The regional government sent out emergency alerts over the weekend and again on Monday, while the rain was falling.

tf.s: Emergency services carried out hundreds of rescues.
tf.why: They carried out about 500 rescues in the Valencia region, and helicopters lifted many people from rooftops.

tf.s: The floods brought back memories of the deadly 2024 floods.
tf.why: The floods brought back painful memories of October 2024, when more than 230 people died.

tf.s: The rain grew stronger as the week went on.
tf.why: The rain began to die down on Tuesday, but warnings stayed in place in nine provinces.

lines.text: Did you see the news from Spain? Storm Adam hit the east coast.
I saw some videos. The floods {{washed cars away}}. It was [[hard to watch]].
Some towns got more than 600 millimeters of rain in one day.
That's about two feet of rain! Did people get hurt?
News reports count at least four deaths. Some say five.
That's so sad. Were a lot of people trapped?
Yes. The water {{cut off}} several towns, and people waited on their roofs.
Many by helicopter. Emergency services {{carried out}} about 500 rescues.
I bet some of those people were saved [[in the nick of time]].
Probably. And a shelter in one town {{took in}} about 400 people overnight.
Did officials warn people before it got bad?
Yes. They {{sent out}} phone alerts and told people in about 145 towns to {{stay in}}.
Good. It's smart to be [[on the safe side]].
For a lot of people, this {{brought back}} memories of 2024. The warnings came late that time.
So it sounds like they've [[come a long way]] since then.
Maybe. The rain started to {{die down}} on Tuesday.
That's good news. Still, those towns have [[a long road ahead]].
